name: Burg Bruck
kurzbeschreibung: Schloss Bruck in Lienz – medieval castle residence of the Counts of Görz with a massive keep, Romanesque double chapel, and the world’s largest Albin Egger-Lienz gallery.
beschreibung:
Overview

The commanding Schloss Bruck rises upon a prominent forested hill at the western edge of Lienz, serving as the proud landmark of East Tyrol's district capital. Constructed between 1252 and 1277 as the fortified residential seat of the powerful Counts of Görz, the complex looks back upon more than seven centuries of rich history. A massive five-storey keep, heavy surrounding curtain walls, and the Romanesque palace building bear testimony to medieval grandeur. An artistic jewel of exceptional significance is the two-storey Castle Chapel of the Holy Trinity, adorned with vibrant late-Gothic frescoes by master Simon von Taisten. Today, the castle houses the acclaimed Museum of the City of Lienz, exhibiting the world's most extensive collection of artworks by celebrated Tyrolean painter Albin Egger-Lienz.

Route & Requirements

From the car park at the base of the hill, a shaded, well-maintained footpath leads through the castle park to the main gate (roughly 10 to 15 minutes' walk). The spacious inner courtyard and the ground floor of the museum are easily accessible, whereas the historical keep and upper exhibition chambers are reached via historical stone stairs and wooden flights (limited wheelchair accessibility). Sturdy, comfortable walking shoes are recommended for ascending the tower and exploring the battlements. Nature lovers can combine their museum tour with a tranquil stroll around the castle pond, surrounded by ancient park trees. Families benefit from specialised interactive children's discovery booklets and medieval-themed tours.

Visit & Arrival

Museum Schloss Bruck is open from late May to mid-October from Tuesday to Sunday between 10:00 and 16:00; during peak summer in July and August it opens daily from 10:00 to 18:00. Motorists reach Lienz via the Drautal federal road B100 from Carinthia or the Felbertauern road B108 from Salzburg. Free parking is available directly below the castle grounds. By rail, travel to Lienz railway station, then take local city bus line 1 to the Schloss Bruck stop or walk up in approximately 25 minutes.

Tips

Be sure to climb up to the open-air viewing platform atop the massive keep: the panoramic outlook across the Lienz valley basin and the jagged limestone crags of the Lienz Dolomites is unforgettable. The charming castle café in the historic courtyard invites visitors to relax with traditional East Tyrolean pastries. Admission is free with the Osttirol Card.
preis: Adults €12.00, children/students (6–18) €2.50, family ticket €24.00; free with Osttirol Card
oeffnungszeiten: Late May to mid-October: Tue–Sun 10:00–16:00 (July & August daily 10:00–18:00)
